The New Arab: UKMTO says 2 tankers struck in Hormuz

categories.summary: The UK maritime agency (UKMTO) confirmed a tanker was attacked and caught fire off the UAE coast on 23 November, with no injuries. Iran's navy says more tankers hit mines and burned on 23-24 November (its own claim). A Houthi strike hit a tower in Riyadh on 24 November, injuring 11 (Saudi civil defence). Iran claims it badly damaged US bases, with no independent confirmation; no new confirmed attacks on US bases since 21 November. Taiwan and Korea are quiet.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal. Forecast markets give a Russian or US nuclear test this year only about 2-3%.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: Washington Examiner: Chinese state hackers used AI
SC World: Chinese actors use AI tools for automated attacks

categories.summary: US reports say hackers, suspected to be China-linked, used AI tools to break into CIA and US intelligence analysis systems (unclassified data); this fits the suspected China campaign the collector rates strong and touching Australia, but no Australian attack in it is confirmed. The Wall Street Journal reports up to 50 ships may have been hit by cyber attacks in the Gulf, with Iran the main suspect (not officially confirmed). Some linked items (a deepfake video in India, general AI-hacking articles) are not attacks. Australian phones, banks and the grid are normal.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.summary: WHO reports bird flu (H5N1) in the United States, Ebola in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria, and MERS in Qatar; none is spreading toward Australia. No Adelaide emergency departments are very busy.

categories.name: Natural hazards

sources.title: Bureau of Meteorology: SA fire danger ratings

categories.summary: Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges is High today and Moderate tomorrow (about 28°C, gusts near 40 km/h). No fire bans, CFS warnings or Watch and Act messages; 13 fires are active across SA, including two small grass fires in the Hills (Highland Valley and Carey Gully) with no warnings. Some outback roads are still closed by flooding. Light rain possible Friday.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply

sources.title: Khaleej Times: Oil falls almost 5% as Trump signals restraint on Iran

categories.summary: Hormuz is still effectively shut (100+ ships a day before the war; about 3 a day now). Brent oil fell another 4% to about US$88 and SA pump prices are a couple of cents lower than last week. Supply is tight but there are no shortages in SA.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: US chip shares fell almost 8% and South Korea's share market dropped 5%, triggering a brief trading halt there. The US 'fear gauge' (VIX) is about 26 and gold eased. The Australian dollar is about 66 US cents. No sign of bank trouble in Australia.

drivers: A run of big overseas hacks and outages continues: US reports now say China-linked hackers used AI tools to get into CIA and US intelligence systems, after the EU Commission, Visa/Mastercard/JPMorgan suppliers, the FBI crime database, Chase, Apple and Microsoft. None has hit Australian banks, phones or power.

If the China-linked hacking is one deliberate campaign, the likely aim is quiet footholds in allies' phone, power and water networks ahead of any Taiwan crisis, with phone networks, utilities and ports the likely next targets; this is a hypothesis, though governments have blamed China for parts of it.
Suspected Iran-linked attacks on shop freezers, small water systems and possibly ships in the Gulf remain overseas.

headline: Tanker attacks in Hormuz go on but nothing new has hit US bases; the Hills cool to Moderate fire danger tomorrow.
summary: The UK maritime agency confirmed another tanker was hit and set on fire off the UAE on Monday, with no injuries; Iran says more tankers hit mines but that is its own claim. No new confirmed attacks on US bases, and oil fell again to about US$88. US reports say China-linked hackers used AI tools to get into CIA and US intelligence systems; no Australian services are affected. Fire danger in the Hills is High today and drops to Moderate tomorrow; two small grass fires in the Hills are being handled with no warnings.
